drafts.title: Under AI product launch packets that gloss over data privacy or compliance.
drafts.text: The hidden cost of any new AI feature isn't the inferencing; it's the trust boundary you just crossed. Who audits the data flow, who owns the model output, and who gets blamed when it leaks? Budget for that before you ship.

drafts.title: Under devtool or platform launch packets where lock-in is relevant.
drafts.text: The hard way to pick a developer platform: don't look at the feature list. Look at the exit cost. If migrating off takes more than a sprint, you're not choosing a tool—you're choosing a landlord.

drafts.title: Under consumer app growth or distribution strategy packets.
drafts.text: Brutal truth: most consumer apps don't fail because of bad UX. They fail because the distribution channel owns the user. If you can't reach them outside the app store, you're renting your audience.

drafts.title: Under Big Tech platform policy or API change discussions.
drafts.text: Startup strategy in one rule: if your product's value depends on a platform staying open, you're not building a company—you're building a feature. Platforms change defaults when it suits them.
